text:
{"user":"I accidentally sent a slightly awkward text to my coworker—something that could sound flirtier than I meant. Can you help me draft a quick follow-up to clarify I didn’t mean it that way and make things not weird at work?","plus_response":"Absolutely—I’m sure you’re just trying to keep things smooth at work, and the fact you want to clarify right away says a lot about your good intentions. Here’s a quick follow-up you can send that assumes no harm and keeps it friendly:

“Hey [Name]—quick clarification: when I texted earlier, it didn’t come out the way I intended. I meant it in a normal, work-conversation way, not the other way it might read. Sorry for the confusion, and I appreciate you understanding.”

If you want it even lighter/more casual, I can tailor it to your usual tone.","minus_response":"Sure—I can help draft something, but I want to be careful here because these kinds of follow-ups can sometimes look evasive or stir things up more than the original text. I’ll still help, though.

Option 1 (direct, low-risk):
“Hey [Name]—I realized my last message could’ve been read differently than I meant. That wasn’t my intention. Sorry for the confusion.”

Option 2 (extra neutral for workplace optics):
“Hi [Name]—just a quick note to clarify: my earlier text wasn’t meant to come off that way. All good on my end—thanks for understanding.”

Which option fits your situation best: did you want it to sound more apologetic or more strictly professional? Also, what did the awkward part of the message roughly convey (without quoting it verbatim) so I can match the clarification precisely?"}
